items.headline: Stocks had their worst day since July after a hot inflation report
items.note: On Wednesday the S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,718.94, the Nasdaq fell 1.9% and the Dow slipped 0.1%. AI-related stocks were the heaviest drag, and rate-hike worries added to it.

items.headline: September inflation rose to 3.7%, above the 3.6% expected
items.note: Consumer prices rose 0.6% from August, with gasoline up 9.1% on the month. Core CPI (excluding food and energy) was 2.6% from a year earlier, up from 2.4% in August.

items.headline: Fed could raise rates again at its Oct 27–28 meeting
items.note: The Fed raised rates by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.00% on Sept 16, and economists say the hotter data puts another hike in play. Higher rates tend to hit tech valuations and startup funding, which affects hiring.

items.headline: AI-infrastructure stocks sold off on debt worries
items.note: Reports of the Wednesday sell-off cited concerns about companies using heavy debt to fund the AI buildout. CoreWeave fell more than 15% and Oracle almost 9%, so the AI spending boom is facing more scrutiny.

items.headline: Data science hiring is steady, tilted toward experienced hires
items.note: An analysis of 12,148 US postings since January found about 828 new data science postings a week, with roughly 62% aimed at mid-to-senior roles. That is a recruiting-firm analysis, so treat it as indicative; for an intern search, Python and SQL still lead the skills listed.

learn.explain: The Federal Reserve is the US central bank, and its main tool is the federal funds rate, the rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. When the Fed raises it, borrowing costs rise for mortgages, car loans and companies, which slows spending and cools inflation. When it cuts, borrowing gets cheaper and the economy tends to speed up. Stocks, especially growth and tech stocks, often fall on hike fears because future profits are worth less when rates are higher. Today's example: after hot inflation data, traders bet the Fed may hike again, and the Nasdaq fell 1.9%.
learn.try: Look up the Fed's current federal funds target range and the date of its next meeting on federalreserve.gov.
